title: Sales enablement prospect playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Diego Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is designed for Redwood Inference account teams and AE/SDR motions engaging enterprise prospects. It consolidates positioning and messaging, concise competitive brief(s), a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, two short case studies, and a security FAQ for prospects. Use this as a canonical reference for discovery calls, technical validation, and procurement conversations.

One-line positioning

- Redwood Inference: a production-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-effective, and secure across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Key target personas and value propositions

- Platform/Infra Engineer: predictable throughput, autoscaling reserved capacity, GPU-efficient runtime, and integrations with existing IaC.
- ML Engineer: consistent model serving across dev/prod, versioned rollouts, quantization & inference performance recommendations.
- Product Manager/Engineering Leader: lower per-token costs through batching/caching, reliability SLOs, and clear rollback/rollout controls.
- Security/Compliance Officer: private VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging and SOC/ISO compliance evidence.

Core product messages (bus-sell bullets)

- Unified runtime across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — same API, same observability.
- Production-first controls: canary rollouts, per-route SLOs, and automatic fallbacks to preserve availability.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that meaningfully reduce GPU token cost without regressing quality.
- Enterprise readiness: reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed latency/uptime targets, and compliance integrations for regulated workloads.

Competitive brief (priority competitors and how to position)

1) Large cloud AI platform (C1) – common objections: "We already have endpoints in the cloud."
   - Positioning counter: differentiate on unit economics + observability. Redwood reduces per-token cost for bursty production workloads via continuous batching and prefix caching; we provide transparent token-level cost breakdowns per route (unlike many managed endpoints which lack fine-grained cost attribution).

2) LLM API provider (C2) – common objections: "Their models are simpler to use and cheaper."
   - Counter: emphasize deployment modes and SLAs. For customers needing predictable throughput and enterprise controls, Redwood Dedicated/Private provides reserved capacity and compliance packages that general LLM APIs do not. Offer MLP (migration) plan with a pilot to prove parity on latency and cost.

3) Self-hosted inference vendors/open-source runtimes (C3) – objection: "We can self-host and optimize cheaper."
   - Counter: highlight operational burden and ROI. Redwood combines an optimized serving runtime, kernel selection, and orchestration so your team avoids months of ops work. Showcase our benchmarked latency/cost numbers for target workloads and offer a TCO comparison worksheet.

4) Niche vertical competitors (e.g., domain-specialized vendors) – objection: "They claim domain expertise."
   - Counter: emphasize that Redwood supports custom model onboarding, versioning, and quality monitoring tied to prompt/eval sets; combine with solution partners to deliver vertical expertise while we operate inference.

Battlecards (quick soundbites for AEs)

- When to lead with Cost: prospect has bursty traffic, high token spend, or ops teams frustrated by high GPU utilization.
- When to lead with Reliability: prospect requires SLAs, multi-region failover, or predictable latency.
- When to lead with Security: prospect requires VPC/private control plane, on-prem packaging, or strict data residency.

Pitch-deck: recommended slide outline and speaker notes

1) Title / Hook (1 slide): Problem statement — "LLM apps succeed or fail on serving economics and reliability."
2) Customer pain (1-2 slides): show common failure modes (high costs, flakey latency, operational burden).
3) Redwood overview (1 slide): platform modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) + unified API.
4) How it works (2 slides): serving runtime, smart routing, caching/batching, deployment abstraction. Include simple diagram.
5) Performance & cost evidence (2 slides): sample benchmark (throughput, p95 latency) and a high-level cost comparison vs typical managed endpoints and self-host. (Use anonymized customer data where available.)
6) Security & compliance (1 slide): VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC/ISO readiness.
7) Enterprise features (1 slide): reserved pools, autoscaling policies, rollouts, traceable cost per route.
8) Case studies (2 slides): short customer summaries and outcomes (see Case studies section).
9) Pricing & engagement model (1 slide): summary of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and typical procurement paths.
10) Next steps / pilot proposal (1 slide): recommended POC scope, success criteria, timeline.

Slide notes: keep each slide to 3–5 bullets. For technical buyers include an appendix with architecture diagrams and sample API calls.

Pricing guidance & negotiation levers (high-level)

- Hosted API (fastest path): usage-based billing (tokens/embeddings) + optional add-ons for observability retention. Recommend telling prospects: "Start on Hosted to validate product-market fit; move to Dedicated when monthly committed spend exceeds threshold X (example: $30k/month)."
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity: monthly/annual committed contracts for GPU pools. Typical commitments vary by customer size: SMB (<$20k/mo), Midmarket ($20k–$100k/mo), Enterprise (>$100k/mo). Provide a discount matrix for 6/12/24 month commitments.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + dedicated support; typically used by regulated customers. Negotiate multi-year licensing + onboarding/maintenance retainer.

Negotiation and discount levers (examples):
- Volume tiers: scale per-token or per-GPU-hour pricing by committed volume.
- Commitment term: longer commitments yield higher discounts and reserved capacity priority.
- Observability retention: retention beyond standard windows is chargeable separately.
- Professional services: on-prem deployment, SOC evidence generation, and integration work billed as time & materials or fixed-scope.

Internal pricing playbook (what to avoid in early conversations)

- Do not promise unvetted latency SLOs or unlimited burst capacity without SDA approval.
- Avoid deep engineering-level commitments (kernel-level optimizations) during commercial negotiations; defer to solution engineering for technical validation.

Case studies (concise – one paragraph each)

1) FinScribe (fintech scale-up) — Problem: real-time document summarization pipelines with unpredictable daily peaks led to high variance in per-token costs and 95th percentile latency spikes.
   - Outcome: migrated to Redwood Dedicated with intelligent batching and KV prefix caching. Reduced p95 latency from 1.2s to 450ms on typical requests and lowered average per-token inference cost by ~35% within the first quarter.

2) HealthAssist (regulated healthcare SaaS) — Problem: needed private inference to meet data residency and audit requirements while keeping model iteration velocity.
   - Outcome: deployed Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and audit logging. Achieved compliance gating for HIPAA-level review and reduced deployment time for new model rollouts from 6 weeks to 2 weeks using our rollout and versioning tools.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers to common questions)

Q: Where does customer data live and how is it protected?
A: For Hosted customers data is isolated logically and encrypted in transit (TLS1.2+) and at rest. For Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering, private control planes, and on-prem installations. We integrate with KMS/HSM for customer-managed keys.

Q: Do you retain prompts or outputs?
A: Default Hosted retention is configurable; Redwood supports short retention windows for sensitive customers and can disable retention for Private deployments. We provide clear data retention and purge procedures.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness for our control plane; Private/on-prem packages allow customers to maintain their own compliance perimeter. Provide SOC/ISO evidence package on request under an NDA.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: We support KMS integrations (AWS/Azure/GCP) and HSM-backed key storage for private deployments. Keys can be customer-managed for Private and Dedicated options.

Q: How do you handle incident response and notifications?
A: We provide incident SLAs for Dedicated customers, a documented incident response process, and can integrate with customer PagerDuty/Slack channels for real-time notifications.

Q: What security controls exist at the operator level?
A: RBAC for Console and API, single sign-on (SAML/OIDC), audit logs for privileged actions, and role-scoped tokens.

Discovery -> Pilot -> Close: recommended commercial flow (numbered steps)

1) Discovery call (2–4 weeks): define success criteria, target endpoints, representative traffic profile, and data residency requirements. Collect a small prompt set for quality validation.
2) Technical validation (2 weeks): solution engineering runs a pilot on Hosted or Dedicated eval pool. Provide benchmark report (latency, cost, fidelity) and an initial ROI/TCO worksheet.
3) Security review (concurrent): share required evidence, recommend Private demo for regulated customers.
4) Pilot proposal (1–2 weeks): 4–8 week pilot with clear metrics and acceptance criteria (p95 latency target, cost reduction target, availability).
5) Commercial negotiation & procurement (2–6 weeks): propose commitment levels, discounts, and SOW for any professional services.
6) Onboarding & rollout (4–8 weeks): infra setup, SSO/KMS integration, and rollout plan (canary -> A/B -> full).

Appendix: example POC success criteria (table)

- p95 latency target: 2 columns: "Metric" and "Target" (presented as bullet list here):
  - Metric: p95 inference latency, Target: <= 500ms for scoped API route
  - Metric: Average per-token cost, Target: >= 20% reduction vs baseline
  - Metric: Throughput, Target: sustain 200 requests/second burst for 5 minutes without >10% error increase
  - Metric: Security: Encryption at rest/in transit verified, KMS integrated if required

Notes and recommended collateral

- Use the benchmark report template to capture environment, model, sequence length distribution, and kernel/quantization profile used.
- For procurement, provide an anonymized TCO comparison worksheet mapped to the prospect's expected monthly token volume and retention settings.
- If a prospect is primarily concerned about cost, propose a cost-savings workshop with solutions engineering to run model quantization and batching tests on representative prompts.
